title: fix(usage): opening Usage keeps the 7-day totals
subtitle: openclaw/openclaw-windows-node #1821
author: SebTardif
body:
## What Problem

Opening Usage replaces the selected 7-day totals with the 30-day snapshot.

Pull request creation is refused for this account (`CreatePullRequest` FORBIDDEN, REST create 404). The branch is on the fork.

Compare: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/main...SebTardif:fix/f037-usage-period?expand=1

Head: `70a4c754316209006ec493c92bda01df3be167df` on `SebTardif:fix/f037-usage-period`

## User Impact

Usage opens on 7 Days and keeps that period. A 30-day cost that arrived earlier does not move the selector or replace the totals. Choosing 30 Days still requests 30 days.

## Why

The page refresh asked for the selected period and also for a fixed 30-day cost. The first cost payload was applied even when its day count did not match the selector, and the selector then moved to that period. The branch requests status plus the selected period only. A payload applies when its day count is unspecified or within one day of the selection. The handshake may still request 30 days for the rest of the app. That payload does not paint the Usage page while 7 Days is selected.

## Evidence

Before this change, `ShouldApply_RejectsFirstMismatchedResponse` failed: a 30-day payload was accepted for a 7-day selection.

`./build.ps1` succeeded in the worktree. The Usage page sources were saved at 20:11 and the win-x64 exe was written at 20:13 local time on 2026-10-21.

Shared tests passed 4638, skipped 24, total 4662.

Tray tests passed 4462, skipped 0, total 4462. That run includes `UsageCostApplicationPolicyTests`.

## Real Behavior Proof

- Environment tested: Windows, non-dev win-x64 tray from that head, isolated `OPENCLAW_TRAY_DATA_DIR`, fixture gateway on port 61053.
- Commit tested: `70a4c754316209006ec493c92bda01df3be167df`
- Steps: start the tray against the fixture, wait for the handshake cost, then open `openclaw://hub/usage` and read the period selector with UI Automation.
- Evidence: at 20:14:12 the activity log recorded `[usage] 30d usage $0.00`. At 20:15:19 the usage deep link was handled and the log recorded `[usage] 7d usage $0.00`. UI Automation then read Usage selected, `TotalCostText` `$0.00`, `Period7DaysItem` selected true, `Period30DaysItem` selected false, and `DailyEmptyText` `No daily usage for this period`.
- Observed result: after a 30-day handshake payload, opening Usage stayed on 7 Days and showed the applied cost for the selected period.
- Screenshot: no. Evidence is the tray log and the UI Automation selection state.
- Not verified: the fixture total is `$0.00` for every period, so the dollar amount alone does not identify the period. The selector state and the 7-day activity line do. The 30 Days control was not clicked in this run.

## Required proof pools

- `none`: no installer, WSL gateway, MXC, or ARM64 pool applies. The Usage selector trace is above.

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities? No
- Secrets or tokens handling changed? No
- New or changed network calls? No
- Command or tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

comments.body:
Closing as superseded by the Usage implementation merged in #1895 (feat(usage): rebuild the Usage page with the web page's sessions, charts and filters), commit 9d36f5c8bfa0e35d3e33a057d7aa95a3c06cb577. The old first-response policy and AppState cost subscription are gone. Usage now defaults to a seven-day date query, captures the selected range for each request and discards superseded replies; ownership and delayed-response regressions cover that boundary. This is fixed on main, not a claim that the rewrite is already in v2026.11.1. The still-open #1863 (fix(usage): opening Usage keeps the 7-day totals) needs a separate supersession review so its retired page implementation is not reintroduced.
